To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tropical tropospheric warming is strong and smooth, that it is not slowing in recent decades, and that stratospheric cooling has slowed.
tropical warming has not slowed and is consistent with model predictions, and that the subtropical westerlies have strengthened and shifted poleward.
tropical tropospheric temperature trends are as large as expected from climate models, but do not reach as high in the tropical troposphere as expected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection, quantification and attribution of climate change.
the homogenization of the radiosonde data set.

understanding the physical processes that control climate change and variability on all time-scales, and in particular the role of the atmosphere in climate change, including the role of clouds, water vapour and atmospheric circulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the IUK method has now been applied to the full 54-year period of radiosonde data and has revealed no evidence of a slowdown in tropospheric warming, nor any evidence of an increase in stratospheric cooling.

the IUKv2 dataset shows no significant change in the global warming rate since 1979, and no evidence of a slowdown in the tropical troposphere, but that there is a slowdown in the stratospheric cooling rate.
the atmosphere is warming, as predicted by models, but not quite as fast as the models predict.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IUKv2 data show a robust, smooth, and nearly adiabatic warming in the tropical troposphere over the past 50 years.

radiosonde data, when properly treated, support climate model projections of tropical tropospheric warming and of changes in the tropospheric circulation, but do not show a recent slowdown in tropical tropospheric or stratospheric warming.

, despite the large number of radiosonde stations, and despite the large changes in the instruments and measurement procedures, the data can be used with confidence for trend analysis, and that these trends are in broad agreement with model predictions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the challenges of homogenization, the radiosonde record is still a valuable source of information about the evolution of the global climate system.
the IUKv2 dataset, which is freely available, provides a useful tool for analysing the global climate record.

, despite the large number of stations and the many years covered, the radiosonde dataset is still too sparse and noisy to provide definitive information about atmospheric trends, especially in the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere.
